newsitem.title: USA: Goldman sees Fed holding rates steady at Nov FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Goldman sees Fed holding rates steady at Nov FOMC.

text.p: Goldman, Sachs and Co Inc on Friday said it believes the Federal Reserve will leave monetary policy unchanged at the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on November 13.
Goldman also lowered its estimate for third-quarter U.S. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth in light of U.S. trade statistics for August, which were released on Friday, the Wall Street firm said.
"This week's economic news leads us to conclude that the Fed will leave rates steady through November and possibly into early 1997," said Goldman in its U.S. Economics Analyst report.
Goldman cited sluggish third-quarter sales and industrial output, and continued benign inflation as factors supporting its expectation of a steady Fed policy.
Goldman said poor August trade data imply a notably wider third-quarter net exports deficit than it had previously expected.
Therefore, Goldman's estimate of a 2.1 percent annualized real GDP gain in the third quarter now appears too high, it said. A figure closer to 1.5 percent would be more appropriate.
